name: pattern rules over blocks of typed values (COMPASS-REBOL-07, ruled yes 2026-10-30), fixtures first
comment: Written BEFORE any engine. A rule is a C6 list read by the one LOAD, so a grammar is data. Pattern words are UPPER_SNAKE keywords: the types WORD STRING NUMBER KEYWORD PATH PAIR LIST GROUP ROW and SKIP (any one value); END; OPT ANY SOME REPEAT n [m]; OR (ordered choice, as Parse | and PEG /); NOT and AHEAD (look, consume nothing); INTO (descend into a list, a group, a row or a pair -- a pair reads as its key then its value); TO and THRU; COLLECT and KEEP (Parse collect/keep); RULE name (a named rule); MEMBER name (a value drawn from a declared set -- a set is DATA the court collects from the sentence or the world, never code); LIT v (a keyword or any value matched as itself). A lower_snake word, a string or a number in a rule matches itself. A nested list in a rule is a sub-rule. A rule matches only when it consumes its whole input. THE BOUND, refused at declaration: recursion (the named rules form a DAG), a repetition or TO over a rule that can match nothing (so every ANY/SOME turn consumes a value of a finite input: Parse's documented infinite loop cannot be written), a group in a rule (Parse paren!, the host escape), WHILE, DO, and the editing words (CHANGE, INSERT, REMOVE): a pattern judges and never edits. Comments are not values. In the input, list and group items are separated by commas; an item of several values is a ROW (a clause such as CODE "X" is one).

matches.name: a sequence of types
the same sequence, out of order, does not match
OPT: a value that may be absent
ANY then END: every value is a word
ANY then END: a number stops it short of the end
SOME needs at least one
OR: ordered choice, the second alternative taken
literal words as a closed menu: a word outside it does not match
literal words as a closed menu: a word inside it matches
LIT matches a keyword as itself (a bare keyword in a rule is a pattern word)
INTO descends into a list: every item a word
INTO: a number among the items does not match
a declaration's shape: DEFINE, its kind, its name, AS, a group of rows, RATIONALE and a string

rules.main: [LIT DEFINE KEYWORD WORD LIT AS INTO [ANY ROW] LIT RATIONALE STRING]

matches.input: DEFINE MENU tones AS (WORDS [plain, formal], CODE "X") RATIONALE "r"

matches.name: a clause is a row of a keyword and one value
a bare string where a clause belongs is not a row
PAIR: a seat list is pairs
INTO a pair reads it as its key and its value
MEMBER: a value drawn from a declared set
MEMBER: a value outside the set does not match

the value join (stzzui's VIBE_STRIPS_RIGHT): every strip is a value some other declaration's list seat holds -- the set is the union of those seats, which the court collects as data and the rule only reads
COLLECT and KEEP: the words kept, the numbers passed over
KEEP outside a COLLECT keeps into the result
TO skips up to what matches, consuming none of it
THRU skips past what matches
NOT: a value that is not a number, every time
NOT: a number stops it
AHEAD looks without consuming
REPEAT n: exactly two words
REPEAT n: three words are one too many
REPEAT n m: between one and two
named rules, referred to and never recursive
a comment is not a value
INTO, three deep
an empty list
a path is one value
items are values, a row is one item: [a b, c] is two items, the first a row
ordered choice commits: the first alternative that matches is taken, and the rest is not tried again

refusals.name: a rule that refers to itself is recursive: refused
ANY over a rule that can match nothing would never end: refused
SOME over a look-ahead consumes nothing: refused
ANY over a named rule that can match nothing: refused
WHILE is refused: a pattern rule is total
a group in a rule is the host escape (Parse paren!): refused
CHANGE is refused: a pattern judges and never edits
a rule that names no pattern
REPEAT with its minimum above its maximum
a pattern word with nothing to apply to
a keyword that is no pattern word
refusals.refusal: FOO is not a pattern word

refusals.name: DO is refused: a pattern rule runs nothing
TO over a rule that can match nothing: it would stop at once and mean nothing
